landmarks.name: Gorée Island
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its role in the Atlantic slave trade and its preserved colonial architecture.

wiki.extract: Île de Gorée is one of the 19 communes d'arrondissement of the city of Dakar, Senegal. It is an 18.2-hectare (45-acre) island located two kilometres at sea from the main harbour of Dakar, famous as a destination for people interested in the Atlantic slave trade.

landmarks.name: African Renaissance Monument
landmarks.writeup: The tallest statue in Africa, symbolizing Africa's emergence from centuries of colonialism and slavery.

wiki.extract: The African Renaissance Monument is a 50-metre tall bronze statue located on top of one of the twin hills known as Collines des Mamelles, outside Dakar, Senegal. Built overlooking the Atlantic Ocean in the Ouakam suburb, the statue was designed by the Senegalese architect Pierre Goudiaby Atepa after an idea presented by President Abdoulaye Wade, and built by Mansudae Overseas Projects, a monument construction company from North Korea.

landmarks.name: Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary
landmarks.writeup: A major bird sanctuary and UNESCO World Heritage site, home to thousands of migratory birds.

wiki.extract: The Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary lies on the southeast bank of the Senegal River in Senegal, in northern Biffeche, north east of St-Louis.

landmarks.name: Lac Rose (Pink Lake)
landmarks.writeup: A salt lake famous for its pink waters caused by algae and high salt content.

wiki.extract: Lake Retba, also known as Lac Rose, lies north of the Cape Verde peninsula in Senegal, some 35 km (22 mi) north-east of the capital, Dakar. It is named for its pink waters caused by Dunaliella salina algae and is known for its high salt content, up to 40% in some areas. Its colour is usually particularly strong from late January to early March, during the dry season. Flooding in September 2022 not only disrupted salt harvesting activities on the lake, but also led the lake to lose its colour, causing a negative effect on tourism. However, as of 2025, the lake has regained some of its colour.

landmarks.name: Saint-Louis
landmarks.writeup: A historic city and former colonial capital with distinctive French colonial architecture.

wiki.extract: Saint-Louis or Saint Louis, is the capital of Senegal's Saint-Louis Region. Located in the northwest of Senegal, near the mouth of the Senegal River, and 320 kilometres (200 mi) north of Senegal's capital city Dakar. It had a population of 254,171 in 2023. Saint-Louis was the capital of the French colony of Senegal from 1673 until 1902 and French West Africa from 1895 until 1902, when the capital was moved to Dakar. From 1920 to 1957, it also served as the capital of the neighboring colony of Mauritania.

cultural_events.name: Dakar Biennale (Dak'Art)
cultural_events.writeup: A major contemporary African art exhibition held every two years in Dakar.

wiki.extract: The Dakar Biennale, or Dak'Art - Biennale de l'Art Africain Contemporain, is a major contemporary art exhibition that takes place once every two years in Dakar, Senegal. Dak'Art's focus has been on Contemporary African Art since 1996.

cultural_events.name: Gambian Wrestling (Laamb)
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional wrestling sport that is a popular cultural and social event.

wiki.extract: Senegalese wrestling is a type of folk wrestling traditionally performed by the Serer people and now a national sport in Senegal and parts of The Gambia, and is part of a larger West African form of traditional wrestling. The Senegalese form traditionally allows blows with the hands (frappe), the only one of the West African traditions to do so. As a larger confederation and championship around Lutte Traditionnelle has developed since the 1990s, Senegalese fighters now practice both forms, called officially Lutte Traditionnelle sans frappe and Lutte Traditionnelle avec frappe for the striking version. This activity predates the modern-day countries of Senegal and Gambia, and Senegambian wrestling is perhaps more historically and geographically correct.

cultural_events.name: Tabaski (Eid al-Adha)
cultural_events.writeup: An important religious festival celebrated with communal prayers and feasts.

wiki.extract: Eid al-Adha is the second of the two main festivals in Islam, alongside Eid al-Fitr. It falls on the 10th of Dhu'l-Hijja, the twelfth and final month of the Islamic calendar. Celebrations and observances are generally carried forward to the three following days, known as the Tashreeq days.

cultural_events.name: Mbalax Music Festivals
cultural_events.writeup: Events showcasing Senegal's popular music genre blending traditional rhythms with modern styles.

wiki.extract: The music of Barbados includes distinctive national styles of folk and popular music, including elements of Western classical and religious music. The culture of Barbados is a syncretic mix of African and British elements, and the island's music reflects this mix through song types and styles, instrumentation, dances, and aesthetic principles.

food_writeup: Senegalese cuisine is rich and diverse, featuring dishes like Thieboudienne (fish and rice), Yassa (marinated chicken or fish with onions and lemon), and Mafé (peanut stew). Meals often combine rice, fish, meat, and vegetables, flavored with local spices and herbs.
brief_history: Senegal was inhabited by various ethnic groups before becoming part of several West African empires. It was colonized by the French in the 17th century and gained independence in 1960. Since then, Senegal has been known for its political stability and cultural vibrancy in West Africa.
current_conflicts: Senegal is generally stable but faces challenges related to border security near the Casamance region, where a low-level separatist conflict has persisted intermittently.

commentary.inflation_management: Senegal's inflation is anchored by the CFA franc's peg to the euro and has been low for most of the period, with deflation in 2014 (-1.1%). The 2008 boom pushed it to 6.2% and the 2022 global shock to 9.7%, the series high, on food and energy prices. It fell back to 0.8% in 2024 and a projected 1.4% in 2025. The BCEAO's regional monetary policy has kept prices stable through the debt crisis, a striking contrast: monetary credibility survived even as fiscal credibility collapsed. But with debt at 130% of GDP, the peg's stability now depends on a fiscal adjustment the government has yet to deliver.
commentary.debt_management: Senegal's debt story was rewritten by scandal. From 17.5% of GDP in 2006 (post-HIPC), the ratio climbed steadily as the Sall government borrowed for infrastructure: the reported figure was 74.4% at end-2023. Then the September 2024 audit by the new Faye government revealed $11-13 billion in hidden debt, and the true ratio was revised to nearly 100% for 2023, reaching 132.4% in 2024, the series high, with 129.7% projected for 2025. The IMF suspended its $1.8 billion program over misreporting, and credit ratings collapsed into junk. A new $2.2 billion IMF program was agreed in principle in 2026. Senegal went in one audit from a manageable borrower to one of Africa's most indebted sovereigns.

key_events.event: Macky Sall won the presidency; infrastructure borrowing began its long climb.
IMF $1.8 billion program approved (June 2023); Sangomar oil field neared production.
March 2024: Bassirou Diomaye Faye won the presidency on a reform platform.
September 2024: government audit revealed $11-13bn in hidden debt; true end-2023 debt was ~100% of GDP, not 74%; IMF suspended its program.
Sangomar oil produced first oil (June 2024); GTA gas neared production.
New $2.2 billion IMF program agreed in principle (2026); ratings remained deep in junk.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The base case is a long, painful workout: oil and gas revenues (Sangomar, GTA) will help, but debt near 130% of GDP requires years of primary surpluses and the political will to sustain them. Upside is a successful IMF program restoring market access; downside is restructuring, which the government has resisted. Uncertainty is high: the hidden-debt revelation destroyed fiscal credibility, and rebuilding it will take longer than the numbers suggest.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
